title: SpaceX Built AI Data Centers So Fast, Some Ran Without Backup Power for Months. Now It Faces a $920 Million Deadline.
author: Matt Dilallo
description: SpaceX has encountered reliability issues while rapidly expanding its AI data center infrastructure, with some facilities operating without backup power and cooling systems for months. The company faces a September 30 deadline to deliver 110,000 Nvidia GPUs to Google under a $920 million/month contract. To address these challenges, SpaceX is reshuffling its data center leadership team with executives from its rocket and Starlink divisions, delaying new projects, and building an in-house turbine blade manufacturing facility to accelerate deployment timelines.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: SpaceX faces significant operational challenges with unreliable data center infrastructure, missed engineering targets, and a critical deadline risk. While the company is taking corrective actions, the execution risks and potential contract jeopardy present near-term concerns for investors.

Google has a $920 million/month contract at stake, but maintains leverage through termination and renegotiation options if SpaceX fails to meet the September 30 deadline. The company's position is protected by contractual safeguards.

title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Reminds Investors with Losses on their Investment in Bloom Energy Corporation of Class Action Lawsuit and Upcoming Deadlines – BE
author: Pomerantz Llp
description: Pomerantz Law Firm has filed class action lawsuits against Bloom Energy Corporation, Primoris Services Corporation, and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc., alleging securities fraud and unlawful business practices. The Bloom Energy lawsuit was triggered by a Hunterbrook Media report alleging the company relies on Chinese scandium in its supply chain, causing the stock to fall 5.67% on July 8, 2026. Investors have until September 28, 2026, to request Lead Plaintiff status.

title: Plug Power Surges 10.1% YTD: Should Investors Ride the Rally?
author: Na
description: Plug Power reported 11.1% revenue growth in H1 2026 driven by strong services and power purchase agreement revenues, along with major electrolyzer orders in Australia and the UK. However, the company posted a $433.5 million net loss, primarily due to convertible debt and warrant liability losses. While the stock underperforms peers and the broader market, its growing presence in green hydrogen and strong electrolyzer demand position it for long-term growth, though analysts recommend current shareholders hold and new investors wait for better entry points.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed fundamentals with positive revenue growth (11.1%) and strong electrolyzer demand, but offset by significant net losses ($433.5M) and underperformance versus industry peers and S&P 500. Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating reflects cautious outlook with long-term potential but near-term concerns.

title: Bloom Energy Outpaces Its Industry in a Month: Time to Buy the Stock?
author: Zacks.Com
description: Bloom Energy (BE) gained 20% in the past month, outperforming its industry and the S&P 500, driven by rising AI data-center demand and a $5B-to-$25B expansion of its Brookfield partnership for AI power infrastructure. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $3.9-$4.2 billion with expected 34% gross margins, though it trades at a premium valuation of 12.94X forward P/S versus the industry average of 4.89X. Despite expensive valuation, Zacks rates it a Strong Buy based on strong earnings performance and superior ROE.
